title.en: Practical 7: Testing a sample for acid or base

text.en: Indicators change colour to tell you whether a sample is acidic or basic.

The aim is to identify the presence of an acid or a base in a given sample. The materials are test tubes, phenolphthalein, methyl orange, sodium carbonate and the sample.
In an acid, phenolphthalein is colourless, methyl orange is pink and sodium carbonate gives brisk effervescence. In a base, phenolphthalein is pink, methyl orange is yellow and sodium carbonate gives no brisk effervescence.
Take 5 ml of the sample in a test tube, add a few drops of an indicator, note the colour change and infer acid or base. Confirm with the other tests.
